claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The equiatomic alloy has limited plasticity associated with its high Mo content.
Heavy cold rolling followed by controlled annealing can improve the alloy's room-temperature compressive strength–plasticity balance without sacrificing its high yield strength.
Room-temperature cold rolling introduces a high dislocation density in NbZrTiHfMo.
Cold rolling refines the grain structure of NbZrTiHfMo.
A limited anneal near 600°C induces partial recovery of the cold-worked microstructure.
A limited anneal near 600°C induces partial recrystallization without full grain coarsening.
Cold rolling and partial recrystallization produce a refined grain structure and tailored dislocation substructure.
Controlled partial recovery balances strain-hardening contributions against ductility-enhancing softening.
The proposed thermomechanical route mitigates the embrittling effects attributed to high Mo content.
The processed alloy will retain a room-temperature compressive yield strength near 1719 MPa.
The processed alloy will exhibit significantly greater compressive plasticity than the as-cast alloy.
The increase in ductility could be approximately twofold or greater.
Complete recrystallization or grain coarsening would compromise the alloy's high strength.
A sufficiently high rolling reduction and controlled annealing time and temperature are required to obtain the proposed strength–plasticity balance.
